title: Eradication dossier generator and redact-validation workflow
creator: Sofia Patel
description:
Problem: Customers and auditors require not only evidence that user data was deleted, but compact, machine-readable bundles that prove removal and the redaction steps applied across services. Current outputs are ad-hoc logs and inconsistent retention markers which complicate audits and increases support load.

Goal: Build an 'eradication dossier' generator that collects provenance, residency stamps, delete/soft-delete/tombstone events, and redaction validations into an immutable, tamper-evident bundle. Provide a deterministic validation workflow that runs post-erase to assert data absence and redaction correctness across copies (backups, analytic sinks, KV caches). The dossier must be exportable by customers and ingestible by auditors, and integrate with existing RTBF orchestration.

Scope:
- Design dossier schema (manifest, proofs, checksums, region stamps, service assertions).
- Implement server-side composer that assembles dossiers after erase workflows complete.
- Build redact-validation runner that replays queries/pattern checks against backups and caches, produces diffs and signed assertions.
- Surface dossier download in Console and via API with audit logs.
- Hook into release pipeline and require security review before GA.
acceptance_criteria: Dossier schema documented in Confluence with field-level definitions and compatibility notes
Server-side composer assembles a dossier in under 60s for a typical tenant batch (<=10k identities)
Redact-validation runner executes cross-service checks and returns a signed validation assertion (pass/fail) with evidence blobs
Console exposes a per-erasure dossier download with tamper-evident checksum and retention metadata
APIs exist to request and retrieve dossiers programmatically; access is logged and audited
Unit/integration tests cover generated assertions and verifier logic; performance regression <10%
Security review completed and findings triaged
tasks: Design dossier schema and provenance model (owner: PM)
Define storage format (compressed JSON + signed manifest) and retention of evidence blobs
Implement composer microservice to collate events from delete-orchestrator, backup-index, and cache sweeper
Build redact-validation runner that supports plugin checks for S3 snapshots, Postgres, KV caches, and analytics exports
Create Console UI: dossier list, download, and verification status
Expose REST endpoints with RBAC and rate limits for dossier requests
Add end-to-end tests and perf benchmarks; include in CI smoke tests
Coordinate security review and finalize signing key ops (KMS/HSM integration)
comments: 2026-01-27 Sofia Patel: Created ticket to centralize auditor-friendly erasure evidence. Initial scope reviewed with Legal and Compliance. Raised question about including raw evidence blobs vs. hashed references.
2026-02-03 Ravi Kumar: Eng grooming - prefer storing hashes + retrieval pointers for large backup artifacts to avoid duplicate storage. Need cross-team contract with Storage and Backups teams.

2026-02-11 Legal (A. Morales): Legal prefers time-stamped region assertions and a signed manifest. Redaction proofs should avoid including PII itself; hashed evidence acceptable if they can request a sealed replay under subpoena.
2026-02-18 Design review (Maya Linn): Suggested 'dossier summary' top-level that shows pass/fail, affected regions, and redaction categories to reduce auditor friction. Console mockups linked.

2026-02-24 Engineering (Ravi Kumar): Prototype composer implemented that gathers delete events and composes manifest. Early perf shows 120s for 5k identities; optimization plan: parallelize backup index reads and incremental checksuming.
2026-03-01 PM feedback (Sofia): Prioritize redact-validation extensibility (plugin model). Add metrics to track validation failure types to drive future automations.
2026-03-04 Security (I. Novak): Preliminary KMS integration OK; will require HSM-backed signing in prod. Raised key-rotation and retention-policy questions; added as follow-up.
2026-03-05 Ravi Kumar: Marking In Progress; end-to-end prototype milestone targeted for 2026-03-25. Noted dependency on ENG-31415 for backup index API stabilization.
notes: Trade-offs discussed: including raw artifacts improves forensic value but increases storage and legal risk; consensus: store hashes + sealed retrieval workflow for exceptional cases
Plan to compress evidence and prefer chunked uploads to avoid long blocking operations during compose
Consider future feature: customer-triggered re-validation and scheduled re-checks for long-tail backups
